summary: Cascading client retries causing apparent inference latency for FluxHealth production traffic
description:
Issue summary:
FluxHealth reports large increase in perceived inference latency and frequent client-side timeouts for their production routes starting 2026-03-10 11:12 UTC. Customer sees 5–20x slower tail latency and many requests fail client-side before any server error is returned.

Impact:
- All FluxHealth production routes in us-east show user-visible slow responses for ~45 minutes.
- Business impact: downstream patient-facing feature degraded; customer flagged as Sev1.
- Traffic volume for this tenant is ~2.5x normal during window; Spike correlated with batch job from FluxHealth but their team says job is within expected parameters.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted API (prod) in us-east
- Customer account: fluxhealth-prod (enterprise)
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sends steady traffic from fluxhealth-prod to text-generation route using redwood-13b-v2.
2) When rate limits hit (429s) the FluxHealth client SDK performs immediate retries with short exponential backoff (base 200ms).
3) Retries amplify traffic and cause the gateway rate limiter to throttle more aggressively, appearing as increased latency and client-observed timeouts.
4) Can be reproduced in staging by replaying FluxHealth traffic trace with same client retry config and enabling strict rate limiter on gateway.
logs:
- Gateway logs: surge of 429 responses from rate-limiter at 2026-03-10T11:12:34Z (see grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/surge/fluxhealth-429)
- Serving runtime logs: increased queue depth and batching spikes; head-of-line blocking observed on several pods.
- Datadog traces: delayed service entry spans on api-gateway -> router (trace id sample: 2f7a3b)
- Example log lines copied to S3: s3://redwood-support/fluxhealth/SUP-91561/logs-11-12-2026.txt
investigation_notes:
- Initial triage (Aisha): confirmed customer-side timeouts correlate with a burst of 429s from gateway.
- Observed pattern: client does aggressive immediate retries for 429s; these retries arrive as fresh requests (not recognized as retries by gateway) and contribute to sustained higher load.
- Hypothesis: combined effect of tenant-level quota enforcement + client retry behavior caused transient overload and queueing in serving runtime, increasing p95/p99 token latencies.
- Confirmed by replay: after simulating client retry loop, p99 token latency increased from ~300ms to ~2.1s and 429 rate rose by 3x.
- Checked recent deploys: no serving-runtime deploy at the incident start time; api-gateway PR #451 (rate-limiter tuning) deployed 4 hours earlier but config unchanged for this tenant.
- Related internal ticket INT-412 tracks gateway rate-limiter observability gaps.
mitigation:
Short-term: coordinated with FluxHealth to throttle their retry behavior — asked them to switch client SDK to exponential backoff with jitter and increase initial backoff to 800ms. This immediately reduced retry amplification.
Medium-term: implement token bucket hold-back and retry-aware headers at gateway so retries are recognized and treated with lower priority, and introduce per-tenant cooldown windows for quota throttling.
Immediate operational action taken: enabled conservative rate-limiter policy for fluxhealth-prod for 30 minutes starting 2026-03-10T12:05Z to allow backlog to drain.
Workaround for customer: patched SDK (v1.2.7) with jittered backoff and retry budget; FluxHealth deployed patch at 2026-03-10T12:22Z and reported error rates dropping by ~80%.
resolution_notes: Pending longer-term work. Owner: Rate-limiter team (Miguel). Planned follow-ups: PR to add X-Client-Retry header propagation and priority handling, add tenant retry budget metrics to syslog, and update customer runbook for recommended SDK retry settings. Target ETA for fixes: 2026-03-24.
